name: Luxor International Airport
before:
The airport for Luxor, 6 km east of the city, and the practical arrival for the Valley of the Kings and for anyone joining a Nile cruise. A lot of the traffic is charter.

It is much bigger than the town suggests. An upgrade in 2005 lifted capacity to eight million passengers a year, with 48 check in desks, eight gates and five baggage belts.

The passenger facilities are unusually complete: a bank, a bureau de change and a cash machine, restaurants and cafeterias, a VIP lounge, duty free, a chemist, a newsagent, a gift shop, a travel agency, a tourist help desk, car hire, first aid, a baby and parent room, a business centre and step free access throughout.

On the freight side there is refrigerated storage, animal quarantine and livestock handling, with EgyptAir Cargo as the handling agent.
after: The airport for Luxor, about 6 km east of the city, used by visitors to the Valley of the Kings and by passengers joining Nile cruises. Charter and holiday airlines fly in, and tour operators sell flights packaged with week-long Nile cruises.
